title: Salivary RANKL and OPG gene expression quantification during intermaxillary elastic traction in orthodontic patients☆
author: Siva Dharma, Nasir, et al.

steps.title: Collect unstimulated saliva
steps.instruction: Instruct participants to abstain from eating, drinking, chewing gum, or oral hygiene for ≥1 hour; seat them upright; let saliva pool naturally and expectorate into a sterile 50 mL polypropylene tube using the passive drooling method until ~5 mL is collected; use a timer (≈5 min) to standardise sampling duration.

steps.title: Cool and freeze samples
steps.instruction: Immediately place the collected saliva on ice, transport on ice to the laboratory, and store at –80 °C without centrifugation.

steps.title: Thaw and homogenize saliva
steps.instruction: Thaw samples on ice and vortex thoroughly to ensure homogeneity.

steps.title: First centrifugation and resuspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the thawed saliva at 10,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C using a refrigerated micro‑centrifuge (Hettich Mikro 220R). Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL cold physiological saline (0.9 % NaCl, RinsCap® NS, Malaysia), and vortex until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Three‑wash pellet purification
steps.instruction: Repeat the following wash cycle two more times (total of three washes): centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL cold 0.9 % NaCl, vortex. After the third wash retain the purified pellet for RNA extraction. All steps are performed promptly at 4 °C.

steps.title: Extract total RNA
steps.instruction: Using the innuPREP RNA Mini Kit 2.0 (IST Innuscreen GmbH, Berlin, Germany), follow the manufacturer’s protocol with a modified final elution volume, keeping all handling at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Wash 1: add 500 µL high‑salt wash buffer, centrifuge 11,000 × g for 1 min.
Wash 2: add 700 µL low‑salt wash buffer, centrifuge 11,000 × g for 1 min.
Additional wash: add 80 % ethanol, centrifuge 11,000 × g for 1 min.
Elute RNA (volume as per modified protocol).

steps.title: Run RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Program the thermal cycler as follows: initial denaturation at 95 °C for 10 min; 49 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s denaturation followed by 60 °C for 1 min annealing/extension with fluorescence acquisition; melt‑curve analysis from 65 °C to 95 °C in 0.5 °C increments, holding 5 s at each step with continuous fluorescence acquisition. Accept only reactions showing a single sharp melting peak.

steps.title: Calculate relative expression
steps.instruction: Obtain Ct values automatically with the CFX Maestro fluorescence‑threshold algorithm and use the mean of technical duplicates. Compute ΔCt = Ct(target) – Ct(β‑actin); ΔΔCt = ΔCt(time point) – ΔCt(T0 baseline); Fold change = 2^(–ΔΔCt). Calculate the RANKL/OPG ratio from the respective fold‑change values. Verify melt‑curve criteria before inclusion.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of data
steps.instruction: Analyze the dataset with IBM SPSS Statistics v25.0 and GraphPad Prism v10.0.0. Fit linear mixed models with malocclusion group (Class I/II/III) as a between‑subject fixed effect, time point (T0/T1/T2) as a within‑subject fixed effect, and patient identity as a random intercept. Obtain estimated marginal means and 95 % confidence intervals; perform Bonferroni‑adjusted pairwise post‑hoc contrasts (p < 0.05). Report effect sizes as partial η² and Hedges’ g. Assess baseline age and BMI comparability with Kruskal‑Wallis tests.

description: The protocol was validated through application to 90 salivary RNA samples from 30 orthodontic patients (10 per group). RNA extraction yielded a mean concentration of 277.1 ± 270.1 ng/µL (median 178.9 ng/µL; range 13.8–1373.0 ng/µL), with mean A260/A280 of 1.96 ± 0.09 and mean A260/A230 of 2.01 ± 0.34, consistent with high-quality nucleic acids suitable for RT-qPCR. All 90 included samples exceeded the minimum concentration threshold of 13.3 ng/µL. 13 samples from 6 patients were excluded at the RNA quality assessment stage as the RNA concentration was insufficient for reliable reverse transcription, and these patients were omitted from all subsequent cDNA synthesis, RT‑qPCR, and statistical analyses. β-actin demonstrated stable Ct values across study groups and all three time points (mean 24.27 cycles; SD 2.24 cycles), confirming its suitability as an internal reference for normalisation of RANKL and OPG gene expression in this cohort. Melt curve analysis confirmed single, sharp melting peaks for all included RANKL and OPG reactions. No-template controls showed no amplification, excluding reagent contamination and primer-dimer artefacts.
